cards.front: What is the first pillar of Islam?
cards.back: Shahada - the declaration of faith that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger

cards.front: What is the second pillar of Islam?
cards.back: Salah - the five daily prayers performed at specific times throughout the day

cards.front: What is the third pillar of Islam?
cards.back: Zakat - the obligatory charity given to the poor and needy (2.5% of wealth annually)

cards.front: What is the fourth pillar of Islam?
cards.back: Sawm - fasting during the month of Ramadan from dawn to sunset

cards.front: What is the fifth pillar of Islam?
cards.back: Hajj - the pilgrimage to Mecca that every able Muslim must perform once in their lifetime

cards.front: What is the holy book of Islam?
cards.back: The Quran - the divine revelation received by Prophet Muhammad over 23 years

cards.front: Who is the final prophet in Islam?
cards.back: Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) - the last messenger sent by Allah

cards.front: What is the name of the Islamic calendar?
cards.back: Hijri calendar - based on the migration (Hijra) of Prophet Muhammad from Mecca to Medina
The Arabic word for God - the one and only deity in Islam
Submission to the will of Allah - the religion of peace and submission
One who submits to Allah - a follower of Islam
The teachings and practices of Prophet Muhammad - the second source of Islamic law
Sayings and actions of Prophet Muhammad - recorded traditions and teachings
Islamic law - the legal framework based on Quran and Sunnah
Faith - the six articles of faith in Islam
Oneness of Allah - the fundamental belief in the unity of God
The Hereafter - life after death and the Day of Judgment
The Day of Resurrection - when all people will be judged by Allah
Paradise - the eternal reward for righteous believers
Hell - the eternal punishment for disbelievers and sinners
Angels - spiritual beings created by Allah to serve Him
Books - the divine scriptures revealed by Allah to various prophets
Messengers - prophets sent by Allah to guide humanity
Divine Decree - Allah's predestination and knowledge of all things
Supplication - personal prayer and communication with Allah
Remembrance of Allah - the practice of remembering and praising Allah
Glorification of Allah - saying 'Subhan Allah' (Glory be to Allah)
Praise of Allah - saying 'Alhamdulillah' (Praise be to Allah)
Magnification of Allah - saying 'Allahu Akbar' (Allah is Great)
Declaration of Allah's unity - saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' (There is no god but Allah)
Seeking forgiveness - asking Allah for pardon and mercy
Repentance - turning back to Allah and seeking forgiveness for sins
Patience - enduring difficulties with faith and perseverance
Gratitude - being thankful to Allah for His blessings
Trust in Allah - relying on Allah while taking necessary actions
Excellence - doing good deeds with sincerity and perfection
Justice - fairness and equity in all dealings
Trust - fulfilling responsibilities and keeping promises
Truthfulness - being honest and sincere in words and actions
Modesty - having a sense of shame and decency
Generous - being kind and giving to others
Permissible - what is allowed in Islam
Forbidden - what is prohibited in Islam
Disliked - what is discouraged but not forbidden in Islam
Recommended - what is encouraged but not obligatory in Islam
Obligatory - what is required in Islam
Compulsory - what is mandatory in Islam
Recommended - what is encouraged based on Prophet's practice
Voluntary - what is optional in Islam
Neutral - what is neither encouraged nor discouraged in Islam
Independent reasoning - the process of deriving Islamic law from sources
Consensus - agreement among Islamic scholars on a matter
Analogical reasoning - deriving law by comparing similar cases
Juridical preference - choosing the better option when multiple solutions exist
Public interest - considering the welfare of the community in legal decisions
